mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.02) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals a bottoming process in the residential demand cycle, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism reverses when unemployment exceeds 8%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.02) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.03) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance, which immediately raises risk-free rates and equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.01) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when market volatility (VIX) exceeds 30.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a precautionary savings behavior, which typically precedes a consumer spending rebound and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous 3-month average AND GDPC1 < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.01) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment spikes above 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.02) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when wage growth exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for four consecutive months signals a deepening housing slump, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.02) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when mortgage rates fall below 4%.
